newsitem.title: INDIA: India police fire at violent mob, 10 dead.
newsitem.headline: India police fire at violent mob, 10 dead.

text.p: At least 10 people, including two children and a woman, were killed when police opened fire on a crowd protesting at the desecration of a social activist's statue on Friday, police said.
Earlier, hospital sources had put the number of casualties at 11 in the incident in Bombay, India's main commercial city.
Police said trouble started when a statue of Bhimrao Ambedkar, a revered leader of the lower social classes, was found garlanded with shoes, viewed as an insulting gesture.

Leaders of opposition parties in India's western state of Maharashtra, of which Bombay is the capital, have called for a one-day strike on Saturday to protest at the incident, which will be probed by a judge, government officials said.

Gopinath Munde, Home (interior) Minister of Maharashtra, said the demonstrators, who gathered at the statue early on Friday morning, turned violent and started burning vehicles, prompting police to open fire at them.
He said the mob tried to set fire to five trucks, three of them loaded with liquefied petroleum gas and one each carrying diesel and petrol.
Munde said the police opened fire at the protestors, whose numbers swelled to more than 4,000, only after they failed to disperse them by caning.
"If the five trucks had been set on fire they would have damaged an area of at least three to four square kilometres (one to 1.5 sq miles)," Munde said.

Bombay's northeastern suburb of Ghatkopar where the shootings occurred, about 15 kms (10 miles) from the city centre, was particularly prone to violent reactions to such slurs on the dead leader, Munde said.
"This area is known for reacting to such incidents in other places," he said. Protestors threw stones at passing vehicles and torched two buses after forcing the passengers to get off, he added.
Demonstrators accused police of indiscriminate firing during what they said was an orderly protest at the slum suburb of Ramabai Colony.
"We were making a silent protest by stopping vehicles on the highway when two vans of special armed police arrived," said Satish Balerao, 25, one of the protesters.
"They scrambled out and started firing indiscriminately," he said. "They did not give any warning. There was no lathi (cane) charge...no warning shots."
The dead included an 11-year-old boy and a 12-year-old girl -- both apparently bystanders -- and an elderly woman.
Twenty-five were wounded and treated in hospital.
Twelve-year-old Mangala was shot dead as she crossed the road, witnesses said.
Lunch boxes carried by victims on their way to work lay strewn on the road, eyewitnesses said.
"My brother, Bablu, was standing at the door. He got the bullet directly in his chest. He died instantly," Ravi Chavan, 25, said, sobbing.
Residents said at least four vehicles were set ablaze in the rioting -- but all of them after the police opened fire. A nearby police post was set on fire by crowds, they said.
Ambedkar, known as the father of India's constitution, is treated like a god by the lower social classes in India's rigid Hindu caste system.

Opposition leaders said they were meeting the state's governor to demand dismissal of the state government, ruled by the right wing Hindu militant Shiv Sena and the nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
